decisive_items: expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit
left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
There was no history of endocrine abnormalities
response.rationale: Long-standing fronto-orbital swelling with an expansile bony lesion of the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing in a young woman without endocrine abnormalities favors fibrous dysplasia. The enhancing component reflects fibro-osseous tissue, whereas meningioma more typically causes hyperostosis and osteoma is sclerotic rather than lytic.

rejected.why: The enhancing orbital roof mass could suggest meningioma, but the dominant expansive lytic bony lesion and absence of typical hyperostosis make it less likely.
Orbital osteoma is typically a dense sclerotic lesion, not an expansive lytic bony lesion as described.
